01 / Who I Am

Finding structure in biological variation.

I'm interested in what variation between cells can tell us about genetic regulation. My work brings together statistics, genomics, machine learning, and cellular biology to develop methods for studying that variation.

I want to understand when a model's predictions support a biological conclusion. That means asking how its assumptions shape the result, how uncertainty enters the analysis, and what is lost when heterogeneous cells are reduced to an average.

Across single-cell genetics, RNA velocity, and computational model design, I keep returning to the same question: what can we reliably learn from the data we have?

MPH in Biostatistics at Yale · Gerstein Lab · Columbia research collaboration

02 / Selected Work

Questions into work.

Four connected research stories.

01Single-cell statistical genetics

scPME-QTL

Genetic effects along a cellular continuum.

Pseudobulk analysis can obscure variation between cells; increasingly fine state bins can leave too little information for reliable inference. I developed a mixed-effects framework that works directly with raw counts and continuous cellular states.

  • Poisson GLMM
  • Donor-level reduction
  • Vectorized score tests
Read the research story ↗: scPME-QTL

The question is not only whether a variant has an effect, but where that effect changes.

  1. 01

    Raw UMI counts

    Raw counts and continuous cellular states, without first collapsing cells into pseudobulk samples or discrete state bins.

  2. 02

    Gene-level Poisson null GLMM

    A Poisson generalized linear mixed model, with a donor-level reduction.

  3. 03

    Vectorized score-test inference

    Cis-variant testing under gene-level null models, avoiding a separate alternative-model fit for every variant.

  4. 04

    Static & dynamic cis-eQTLs

    Shared effects and effects that change with cellular context.

scPME-QTL · Analysis at scale

  • 2.8M+single nuclei
  • 388donors
  • 18cell types
  • +20.3%unique eGenes

02Context-dependent genetic regulation

Regulotype

Describing cells through their genetic responses.

I develop statistical models of cell-resolved cis-regulatory effect profiles, asking whether patterns of genetic response across loci can describe cellular context.

  • Latent factor models
  • Cis-response profiles
  • Empirical Bayes
Read the research story ↗: Regulotype

What if a cellular representation reflected how genetic effects change?

03RNA velocity & cellular dynamics

FUSE-Velo

A snapshot can have more than one future.

Different kinetic parameters can fit the same observed snapshot and imply different cellular trajectories. I developed a framework that uses future cell populations to constrain those possible dynamics.

  • Kinetic ODE rollout
  • Sinkhorn optimal transport
  • Identifiability
Read the research story ↗: FUSE-Velo

What does a later population reveal that a single snapshot cannot?

04AI for biology & model evaluation

CellForge

Automated models still need scientific judgment.

When repeated model-generation runs produced different architectures and predictive performance, I built an evaluation framework to test generalization to entirely unseen perturbations.

  • Held-out perturbations
  • Generalization
  • Reproducible benchmarks
Read the research story ↗: CellForge

Reliability has to hold beyond the model and setting that worked best.

03 / My Journey

Following the next question.

My path into computational biology has been shaped by a recurring concern about what a model lets us conclude.

Prediction→Inference

  1. 01

    From prediction to interpretation

    NYU Shanghai · Data Science / Artificial Intelligence

    In radiology summarization and image classification, I saw how strong predictive scores could coexist with factual errors or uncertain clinical meaning. Disease-entity evaluation and model visualization made me look more closely at the evidence behind a prediction.

  2. 02

    Giving models scientific structure

    Statistical modeling & scientific machine learning

    Working on a physics-informed neural network for the Buckley–Leverett equation brought physical constraints into the learning problem. I became more interested in how assumptions and structure support scientific interpretation.

  3. 03

    Taking cellular variation seriously

    Yale · Biostatistics & computational biology · Gerstein Lab

    Single-cell statistical genetics gave that concern a biological focus. Developing scPME-QTL took me from model derivation and calibration to questions about how genetic regulation changes along cellular continua.

  4. 04

    Asking what remains uncertain

    Columbia collaboration · Context-dependent regulation · Cellular dynamics

    Regulotype, RNA velocity, and perturbation modeling now connect my interests in latent cellular states, genetic responses, and dynamics. I want to carry uncertainty in those inferred states into the biological conclusions we draw.

Research vision
